_about: A green card under the Cuban Adjustment Act (Pub. L. 89-732; 8 CFR 245.2(a)(2)(ii)) or as a HRIFA dependent (8 CFR 245.15(d)): src/cuban_adjustment.py. The G-28, the I-485 (Part 2, 3.f) and, unless the client doesn't want one, the I-765 (c)(9) in the same envelope (USCIS's CAA page: file it with the I-485 or while it is pending). The evidence in the order of the I-485 Instructions (edition 09/18/26, 'What Evidence Must You Submit', items 2-6, 10-12; the CAA and HRIFA additional instructions): identity, birth certificate, the inspection and admission or parole, the category (Cuban nativity or citizenship and one year of physical presence; for a spouse or child, the principal's proof, the relationship and living together; for a HRIFA dependent, Haitian nationality and the relationship), then court and police records. Mailed to the family-based lockbox (CAA) or the non-family lockbox (HRIFA) for the client's state (USCIS's 'Direct Filing Addresses for Form I-485', updated 12/01/2025). DRAFT: the attorney approves titles and order.
title: Green card under the Cuban Adjustment Act or HRIFA (I-485)

handwork.text: Four identical passport photos (two for the I-485, two for the I-765); the client's name and A-Number lightly in pencil on the back.
Form I-693 (medical exam) in the civil surgeon's sealed envelope. USCIS may reject an I-485 filed without it (I-485 Instructions, item 9).
An inadmissibility ground (a crime, an earlier removal, a J-1 two-year rule): the waiver or other relief goes with the I-485 (Form I-601, I-212 or I-612). The attorney decides.

no_ead._about: The client doesn't ask for a work permit now: the I-485 alone (an I-765 (c)(9) can follow while the I-485 is pending).

exhibits.title: Government-issued identity document with photograph: the passport (for a Cuban principal, the Cuban passport is also proof of Cuban nativity or citizenship)
Birth certificate, with certified English translation (a Cuban birth certificate from the civil registry in Cuba also proves Cuban nativity)
Evidence of inspection and admission or inspection and parole: Form I-94, the parole document, the admission or parole stamp and any U.S. visa
The category: Cuban nationality certificate or citizenship letter; for a spouse or child, the principal's I-485 notice or green card (a HRIFA dependent: the principal's HRIFA approval)
Evidence of physical presence in the U.S. for at least one year: lease, bills, pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns
A spouse or child: the marriage certificate (and the end of any earlier marriage) and evidence of living with the principal
Other identity documents: work permit, Social Security card
Immigration court documents (the Notice to Appear, the judge's orders)

leave_out.intake_questionnaire: The firm's own intake questionnaire: internal.
leave_out.medical_record: Not asked for with the I-485: the medical exam goes in the civil surgeon's sealed I-693.
leave_out.sij_order: A state court SIJ order: a different basis for a green card. Ask the attorney which one this filing is.
leave_out.i360_approval: An I-360: a different basis for a green card. Ask the attorney which one this filing is.
leave_out.declaration: Not asked for with the I-485 under the Cuban Adjustment Act.
leave_out.country_conditions: Asylum evidence, not asked for with this I-485.
leave_out.news_article: Asylum evidence, not asked for with this I-485.
leave_out.photograph: Not asked for with this I-485 (the passport photos go in by hand).
